business: Bracket, a one-person software house based in Kuwait that builds websites for UK small businesses, remotely
by_segment: Sole trader or micro business (1-3 people; income = yearly turnover in GBP)
Established local business (15-40 staff; income = yearly turnover in GBP)
Small team business (4-15 staff; income = yearly turnover in GBP)
why_not: I only hire people another owner I know has used, and this lot are in Kuwait with no clients or reviews to show. Pay-on-approval is clever, but I'm not spending my staff's time briefing a stranger just because it costs nothing upfront.

I check Google and Trustpilot before I ring anyone, and there's nothing to check here: no reviews, no past clients, no UK office. Not paying upfront is nice, but I'd still be giving my time to a company in Kuwait I can't vet, and I don't have time for calls and back-and-forth that might go nowhere.

My Fresha page and Instagram already bring the bookings in, and I knocked up the Wix page myself. I don't see what £655 gets me that I haven't already got, and then they're straight in with £325 a month for SEO.

My Booksy page and Instagram already get me booked, and I knocked up a Wix page myself, so I can't see what a £655 site does that I'm missing. Pay-when-happy is a nice touch but it doesn't solve a problem I actually have.

Paying only when I'm happy is nice, but nothing tells me what I'll be paying every month after launch for hosting, the domain or someone to fix things, and SEO at £325 a month on top is more than I'd spend. They hand me the logins and walk off, and I don't have time to look after a website myself.

I've already got a Fresha booking page that's free and does the job, and Wix is about £15 a month if I want something nicer. £655 to a company in Kuwait with no reviews is a lot when nobody in my Facebook group has heard of them.
why_yes: Normally no reviews and no past clients is an instant no for me after last time, but here I don't pay a penny until the site is finished and I've seen it working on the preview link, so they can't take my money and vanish. I'd try it, cautiously, with the scope nailed down in writing first.
flip: A local owner I trust telling me they built their site and it's been solid for a while.
